comment: VNL-1 sample set: sources, the files fetch.sh downloads and what pack.py makes of them. Picks and layers from the instrument spike (docs/research/instrument-spike-2026-10-24.md on spike/instruments, rounds 1-5). Lengths and seconds are in s.

bigcat.name: Karoryfer Samples x Bigcat Instruments cello

vsco.name: Versilian Studios Chamber Orchestra 2 Community Edition (VSCO-2 CE)
vsco.license_comment: CC0 1.0 Universal as plain text (the Statement of Purpose and sections 1-4, word for word the legal code's, without its header's disclaimer): another file than the other sources' copy, so its own hash

jazz_reamp.name: the Shinyguitar's ten SB_JAZZ notes (shiny, as fetched), re-amped by Sam through a jazz amp and cabinet (2026-11-10: the second take; the first held the raw notes 12 dB down, unprocessed)
jazz_reamp.comment: One local recording (not fetched: copy it to SCRATCH/dl_jazz_reamp/): 44.1 kHz, 16-bit, its two channels identical (summed to mono), the notes in the raw files' alphabetical order, each from silence.

banks.comment: Upright Piano, Knight, vl2 (as heard in the spike), every 10 semitones C#2-D#6. File names sit an octave under MIDI's (C#1 is MIDI 37).
Chromatic one-shots in the SF2's preset 0:0; the spike's roots E2 A2 D3 G3 B3 E4 A4.
mf layer, rr1. The file names are standard pitch (e2 is MIDI 40; measured: no energy an octave below).

The jazz guitar (a candidate lead, 2026-11-10): the Shinyguitar archtop's magnetic pickup (electric), vl2 (velocities 33-64: jazz is played soft), rr1, every minor 3rd A3-C6 (the lead's register); standard pitch (the SFZ's keycenters). At 12 kHz; laid out after the kits (after_kits), so every other zone keeps its place. Three versions (variants; use: the one packed): reamp_pcm, packed (its own note); reamp, Sam's re-amp of the raw notes through his amp and cabinet (the tone: tone.py bypassed) as ADPCM in the bank, ten zones; its cut 0.55 s and a 0.15 s loop (0.1 s put a loop seam on Eb4 and, at 0.12 s, C4), at 12 kHz (16 and 22.05 kHz with the codes searched, 4-8 dB less ADPCM noise, made no difference Sam could hear to the buzz he hears: back to 12 kHz, the bank's room kept for a cello); chain, the raw notes through tone.py's chain (a warm, round, dark jazz box), the first version (2026-11-10).

reamp_pcm.comment: Sam, 2026-11-10: every 4-bit version sounded sub-par next to the plain PCM: the re-amp uncompressed, 16-bit PCM at 12 kHz in the firmware's image (out of the bank: room for a cello), six zones every 6 semitones (A3 C4 Gb4 C5 Gb5 C6: Eb5's attack grit left out), each note within 3 semitones of one from F#3 to Eb6, 0.5 s each (a 0.38 s attack, a 0.12 s loop).

banks.comment: The sampled cello (a candidate lead, 2026-11-11): the Karoryfer x Bigcat cello's sustained bowing (sus), mp (velocities 33-64), the first round robin (_d), every tritone A2-A4 (Sam, after round 1: an octave down, a cello's melody G2-E4, its top A4: F#2 to C5 within 3 semitones of a zone). The file names are an octave under standard pitch (measured: A1_mp_d.wav sounds A2, MIDI 45; the SFZ's keycenters say 33). Straight tone (no vibrato in the take: the sampler's delayed vibrato sings it), so a 0.3 s loop of whole periods holds the bow's sustain. Laid out after the kits (after_kits), so every other zone keeps its place.

The sampled harp (a candidate lead, 2026-11-11, in place of round 1's modal retone: Sam heard an electric piano): VSCO-2 CE's concert harp, mf, every third F4-D6 (the lead's register, Bb4-E6 on the styles' bands: every note within 2 semitones of a zone); standard pitch (measured: A4 sounds 437 Hz). Its attack the pluck and the first 0.6 s of ring, then a short loop the sampler's envelope decays (the harp's own ring: patch.c).

kits_comment: The workbench's sampled kits (wb_drums.c), reduced: from workbench/samples (prep_kits.py's files and kits.json), each piece's layers picked (kits.json's layer indices: the second and the top), the first round robin, at rate, cut to len s (a new hit restarts a lane, so a tail only shows at a phrase's end). Dusty (gogodze) is retired (2026-11-10) and not packed: pack.py keeps its set's index, empty.
